text:
Arrange the following conformational isomers of n-butane in order of their increasing potential energy :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Potential energy rises with torsional strain (eclipsing) and with steric repulsion between the two $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ groups.

I is staggered with the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ groups anti (dihedral angle $180^{\circ }$): least strain, lowest energy.

III is staggered with the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ groups gauche (dihedral angle $60^{\circ }$): slight steric repulsion between the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ groups.

IV is eclipsed with each $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ eclipsing an H (dihedral angle $120^{\circ }$): torsional strain plus $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$/H eclipsing strain.

II is eclipsed with $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ eclipsing $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ (dihedral angle $0^{\circ }$): maximum torsional and steric strain, highest energy.

Increasing potential energy: I < III < IV < II.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift

text: Which of the following is not an example of fibrous protein?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Fibrous proteins are characterized by their elongated, insoluble structure and often serve structural or mechanical roles. Among the options provided, keratin, collagen, and myosin are examples of fibrous proteins.

Albumin, on the other hand, is a globular protein that is soluble in water. It has a more spherical shape compared to the elongated shape of fibrous proteins. Albumin is found in blood plasma and has various functions including maintaining osmotic pressure.

So, the correct answer is:

Option B: Albumin.

text: Spin only magnetic moment in BM of [$Fe(CO)_{4}(C_{2}O_{4})$]$^{+}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Oxalate is $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$ and CO is neutral, so for $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4})]{}^{+}$: $x+4(0)+(-2)=+1\Rightarrow x=+3$.

$\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $[\text{Ar}]3d^{5}$. The four CO ligands are strong-field $π$-acceptors, so the complex is low spin and the five electrons pair up in the $t_{2g}$ set: $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$, with one unpaired electron.


[IMG]

$μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{1(1+2)}=\sqrt{3}=1.73\text{BM}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: The incorrect expression among the following is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) At constant temperature and pressure, $\Delta S_{\text{total}}=-\dfrac{\Delta G_{\text{system}}}{T}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta G_{\text{system}}}{\Delta S_{\text{total}}}=-T$: correct.

(B) $\Delta G^{\circ }=\Delta H^{\circ }-T\Delta S^{\circ }=-RT\ln K$, so $\ln K=-\dfrac{\Delta H^{\circ }-T\Delta S^{\circ }}{RT}$. The expression in (B) sets $K$ itself (not $\ln K$) equal to $\dfrac{\Delta H^{\circ }-T\Delta S^{\circ }}{RT}$ and also drops the minus sign: incorrect.

(C) $\Delta G^{\circ }=-RT\ln K$ gives $K=e^{-\Delta G^{\circ }/RT}$: correct.

(D) For a reversible isothermal expansion or compression of an ideal gas, $w_{\text{rev}}=-nRT\ln \dfrac{V_{f}}{V_{i}}$: correct.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift

text: 1.22 g of an organic acid is separately dissolved in 100 g of benzene $(K_{b} = 2.6 K kg$ mol$^{-1})$ and 100 g of acetone $(K_{b} = 1.7 K kg$ mol$^{-1})$. The acid is known to dimerize in benzene but remain as a monomer in acetone. The boiling point of the solution in acetone increases by 0.17${}^{\circ }$C. The increase in boiling point of solution in benzene in ${}^{\circ }$C is x $\times$ $10^{-2}$. The value of x is $______________. ($Nearest integer) [Atomic mass : C = 12.0, H = 1.0, O =16.0]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With benzene as solvent

$\DeltaT_{b} = i K_{b} m$

$\DeltaT_{b} =$ $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ 2.6 $\times$ $\frac{1.22/M_{w}}{100/1000}$ .... (1)

With Acetone as solvent

$\DeltaT_{b} = i K_{b} m$

0.17 = 1 $\times$ 1.7 $\times$ $\frac{1.22/M_{w}}{100/1000}$ ..... (2)

(1) / (2)

$\frac{\Delta T_{b}}{0.17}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}\times 2.6\times \frac{1.22/Mw}{100/1000}}{1\times 1.7\times \frac{1.22/Mw}{100/1000}}$

$\DeltaT_{b} =$ $\frac{0.26}{2}$

$\DeltaT_{b} = 13$ $\times$ $10^{-2}$

$\Rightarrow$ x = 13
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift

text:
For the reaction A $\to$ B, the rate constant k(in $s^{-1})$ is given by

$\log _{10}k=20.35-\frac{(2.47\times 10^{3})}{T}$

The energy of activation in kJ mol$^{-1}$ is $____________. ($Nearest integer) [Given : $R = 8.314 J K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 31st August Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, 

$\log K=20.35-\frac{2.47\times 10^{3}}{T}$

We know

$\log K=\log A-\frac{E_{a}}{2.303RT}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{E_{a}}{2.303RT}=2.47\times 10^{3}$

$E_{a}=2.47\times 10^{3}\times 2.303\times \frac{8.314}{1000}$ kJ/mol

= 47.29 = 47 (Nearest integer)
